In nine of ten seeds, the readability of those factors fell abruptly and stayed down, nearly always along the same direction in factor space. An Agent layer interprets external scene information, identifies the current regime, selects residual experts, and applies a correction only when recent observed errors support it. New experts enter the pool after they outperform their initializations on a validation set, keeping model growth under explicit control. items.summary: arXiv:2610.33245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data science agents can automate end-to-end machine learning workflows, yet they remain far from competitive on human leaderboards. We propose AdaPRA to address these issues: a persistent coding agent harness that accumulates knowledge across attempts on the same task, with rubric-guided process supervision that identifies and corrects errors. items.summary: arXiv:2610.33684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-evolving training improves the performance of agents on difficult tasks through verifiable feedback, but it often applies costly deliberation uniformly across tasks. items.summary: arXiv:2610.35658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aviation authorities hold decades of accident reports whose narratives record how investigators reconstructed each accident. items.summary: arXiv:2610.34365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Science agents increasingly package domain expertise as reusable skills that plan analyses, select tools, and execute workflows. items.summary: The Maxwell graph of a directed acyclic graph is obtained from its iterated basin and hill boundaries. The unweighted counts of extrema at these levels need not satisfy Morse inequalities. We assign multiplicities by the reduced homology of lower and upper order links and retain the vertices with nonzero local homology. The resulting graph preserves both boundary hierarchies, the local groups, and the homology of all sublevel and superlevel order complexes. Its descending and ascending Morse numbers satisfy the weak and strong Morse inequalities over any field. We also construct a Morse chain complex and compute the local groups in several examples. Finally, we consider homology on the original Maxwell graph and prove analogous inequalities for path homology using relative local groups.

items.summary: Evolution strategies (ES) update a model by sampling a population of perturbed copies, scoring each one, and moving in the reward-weighted direction of the perturbations. items.summary: Many decision-making tasks are inherently multi-objective. Interactive evolutionary multi-objective optimization algorithms (iEMOAs) are particularly well-suited to help the decision-maker find their most preferred solution. However, many of these algorithms employ black-box preference models. For high-stakes decision-making tasks, like healthcare and defense, a high level of transparency is needed, for instance to support accountability. We propose an interpretable iEMOA which uses active learning to efficiently learn a tree-based preference model directly from pairwise comparisons. The survival operator of NSGA-II and NSGA-III is extended with the learned preference model to guide the algorithm towards the region of interest. items.summary: Let $X_2$ be a complex primitive double scheme, $X=(X_2)_{red}$. The ideal sheaf of $X$ is a line bundle on $X$. Let $E$ be a coherent sheaf on $X_2$. Then there exists a nonempty open subset $U$ of $X_2$ and integers $m_1$, $m_2$, uniquely determined by $E$, such that $E_{|U}$ is locally isomorphic to $(O_X\otimes C^{m_1})\oplus(O_{X_2}\otimes C^{m_2})$. If we can take $U=X_2$, we say the $E$ is quasi locally free. If $m_1=1$ we say that $E$ is rigid. In this case, we show that deformations of $E$ are of the same type. So locally free sheaves and rigid quasi locally free sheaves on $X_2$ play the same role on $X_2$ as locally free sheaves do on smooth schemes. In this paper we study the existence and description of quasi locally free sheaves, and flat families of such sheaves.
items.title: Quasi locally free sheaves on primitive double schemes

items.summary: In this paper, we prove a sharp effective Nullstellensatz for projective Cohen-Macaulay schemes of pure dimension over an arbitrary field. In particular, if L is an ample line bundle on a smooth complex projective variety X and J is a coherent ideal sheaf with J\otimes L globally generated, then (\sqrt{J})^{°_L X}\subseteq J. This establishes the sharp bound conjectured by Ein and Lazarsfeld. More generally, we obtain sharp bounds in terms of mixed intersection numbers and a refinement involving products of powers of prime ideal sheaves associated to the irreducible components of the base locus. We also establish sharp radical power bounds for homogeneous ideals in finitely generated standard graded Cohen-Macaulay domains, extending Kollár's sharp effective Nullstellensatz for polynomial rings. items.title: Sharp effective Nullstellensatz for projective Cohen-Macaulay schemes
